subject: Meteorology
title: Eyewall Dynamics
description: A quick, practical guide to Eyewall Dynamics.

hook.text: The eyewall is a ring of the tallest, most powerful thunderstorms on Earth—where the hurricane's peak winds rage.

buildup.text: Warm moist air spirals inward and rockets upward in the eyewall—releasing enormous amounts of latent heat.

discovery.text: This latent heat release is the engine—it lowers surface pressure, which draws in more air, which releases more heat.

twist.text: Eyewall replacement cycles can temporarily weaken a hurricane—an outer eyewall chokes the inner, then contracts.

climax.text: After replacement, the storm often re-intensifies—forecasters watch for these cycles to predict strength changes.

punchline.text: The eyewall is where the storm breathes—shut it down and it rebuilds.

quiz.question: What happens during an eyewall replacement cycle?
options: An outer eyewall forms and chokes the inner one
